subject: Re: [rhipe] plans for compatibility with Hadoop 2.0.x

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] plans for compatibility with Hadoop 2.0.x
parts:
Hello,

You are right, RHIPE works with 0.20 and not Hadoop 2. Fixing RHIPE for Hadoop 2 will make it incompatible with Hadoop 1.  Currently we are rewriting RHIPE, and I guess it will be ready when CDH4 is ready (at Mozilla we use CHD3 and will move to CHD4 sometime in the near future).

This is the most recent RHIPE:

https://github.com/downloads/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/Rhipe_0.70.tar.gz

and for this you'll need to downgrade Hadoop ...

Sorry for that.

Regards
Saptarshi



On Wed, Oct 31, 2012 at 3:56 PM, Christopher Paciorek <christophe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, we had installed CDH4 via Cloudera Manager, which apparently provides Hadoop 2.0.x, on a sets of machines running Ubuntu Precise, R 2.15.1 and Rhipe v.0.69. The datadr.org site says that Rhipe works with Hadoop 1.0.x. And indeed in running the test code at https://www.datadr.org/doc/installation.html#tests, we got an error message when submitting the job (the "rhex(z)" step). (error message below).

Presumably this is because we are running the wrong version of Hadoop. We can go back and install CDH3 from the Cloudera repository (rather than the default CDH4 that is the natural thing to install via the Cloudera manager), but I wanted to check if this was the standard thing to do and to ask if there were plans to have Rhipe be compatible with CDH4/Hadoop 2.0.x in the future.

-Chris Paciorek

Statistical Computing Consultant
Department of Statistics
Univ. of California, Berkeley



map <- expression({
+   lapply(seq_along(map.values),function(r){
+     x <- runif(map.values[[r]])
+     rhcollect(map.keys[[r]],c(n=map.values[[r]],mean=mean(x),sd=sd(x)))
+   })
+ })
z <- rhmr(map, ofolder="/tmp/test", inout=c('lapply','sequence'),
+           N=10,mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0),jobname='test')
rhex(z)
